# PEN-5336 — deliver execution workspace warnings into the pod prompt

Tracking: [PEN-5336](https://paperclip.blockcast.net/PEN/issues/PEN-5336) · follows [BLO-27858](https://paperclip.blockcast.net/BLO/issues/BLO-27858) · PR: [#3313](https://github.com/Blockcast/paperclip/pull/3313)

**Files:** `src/server/job-manifest.ts`, `src/server/job-manifest.test.ts`

BLO-27858 shipped a `SHARED CHECKOUT CONTENTION` warning written for the agent to read before it touches disk. The server computed it, bound it into `context.paperclipWorkspace.warnings`, drained it to the run log — and it reached **no adapter, no pod and no prompt** for four months. The reason is in this file: `buildJobManifest` enumerates `context.paperclipWorkspace` into pod env **explicitly and by name**, nine `setIfPresent` calls, and `warnings` was never one of them. `PAPERCLIP_WORKSPACES_JSON` does not rescue it either — that serialises `context.paperclipWorkspaces`, the **plural** workspace hints, a different object with no `warnings`.

The remedy is server-side (warnings now ride the wake payload's `executionWorkspace`, beside the branch pin, because that payload is the one channel every adapter projects whole and renders into the prompt). Three changes are needed **here** for that to arrive, all in this package's **local** copies of the shared helpers:

1. `renderPaperclipWakePrompt` — this package keeps its own minimal renderer rather than importing adapter-utils', so the shared change does not reach it. It now emits `Execution workspace warning: <text>` lines, and a **warnings-only payload now produces a prompt**: the old `if (!reason && comments.length === 0) return ""` guard returned the empty string for exactly the shape a contention warning arrives on (an unscoped wake has neither). Control characters are stripped in `readWakeExecutionWorkspaceWarnings` because this path reads `context.paperclipWake` **raw** — the local `stringifyPaperclipWakePayload` does not normalize either, so adapter-utils' strip never runs here and a newline inside a warning would forge a prompt line. Bounded at 2000 chars × 10 entries.

2. `shouldUseResumeDeltaPrompt` — **the regression this nearly introduced, and the reason this entry is not a one-liner.** The gate read `wakePrompt.length > 0`. Once warnings render into that string, and they are frequently the only thing in it, a resumed run whose only news was "you are sharing a checkout" would have had its **entire heartbeat prompt replaced by the warning** — delivering the warning would have cost the run its instructions. The gate now reads the payload via a new local `wakeHasResumeDeltaContent`, which returns exactly what the string test returned before warnings existed (reason, or at least one non-empty comment body). A warning is additive, never subtractive. The ten in-repo adapters got the same correction against a new shared `paperclipWakeHasResumeDeltaContent`; this package cannot use that export because it pins a published `@paperclipai/adapter-utils`.

3. `stringifyPaperclipWakePayload` — **the cost the delivery fix pushed onto every other run, found in review.** To keep a *live* warnings array reachable by late writers, the server attaches the execution-workspace patch **unconditionally**, so a run with nothing to say still carries `{"executionWorkspace":{"branchName":null,"warnings":[]}}`. The shared normalizer discards that shape; this package's **local** stringify tests only `=== "{}"`, which it does not match. So every `claude_k8s` pod — including every pure timer heartbeat, which previously had **no wake key at all** — would have been handed a `PAPERCLIP_WAKE_PAYLOAD_JSON` saying nothing, while `skills/paperclip/SKILL.md` tells agents to inspect that variable **first** when present and to read it as a comment wake. A new `wakePayloadWithoutEmptyExecutionWorkspace` strips the empty workspace before serialising. Doing it at **serialisation** time rather than at attach time is what preserves the live-array reasoning in (1): by then dispatch has happened and every late warning is already in the array. The strip is deliberately **stricter** than the shared normalizer, which keys only on `branchName`/`warnings` and drops every other key — this package passes the payload through raw, so an unrecognised key with a value keeps the workspace rather than being silently eaten.

**Rule for the next field added to the wake prompt:** adding to a shared prompt-rendering channel is not additive by default. Anything keyed on *"is the rendered output non-empty"* silently changes meaning. Grep for the gate before you grep for the renderer.

Tests are in `job-manifest.test.ts` under `execution workspace warnings reach the pod prompt (PEN-5336)`, and they deliberately assert against `buildJobManifest(...).prompt` — the string this adapter hands the pod. ⛔ A key-presence assertion on a server-side object is what let BLO-27858 ship green; do not replace these with one. Mutation-checked: deleting the warning projection fails 4 of them, and restoring the old resume-delta gate fails the no-suppression test. The empty-workspace strip in (3) is mutation-checked in both directions: disabling it fails the timer-heartbeat case, and widening it to drop the workspace unconditionally fails all three "a real warning / branch pin / future field survives" cases.

**Known residual, filed as [PEN-5349](https://paperclip.blockcast.net/PEN/issues/PEN-5349), deliberately not fixed here.** The local renderer drops far more than warnings relative to the shared one: the branch pin, issue status/work-mode/priority, blockers, tree holds, checkbox selections, annotation deltas, and the **planning directive** — which is a prohibition (`Do not write code or perform implementation work`). Every seat on this fleet runs `claude_k8s`, so none of that reaches a prompt today. Closing it changes every `claude_k8s` prompt in the fleet, including this same resume-delta gate, and wants its own change. A comment on the renderer records it.
